Sampling lists for every perceiver

Source: R/psn.R
psn_sample.Rd

For each person in an unweighted, undirected network, draws a stratified list of real and counterfactual relationships from their social orbit. This calls samplenetwork in SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl; see its documentation for the procedure, the carryover rule and the consent rules.

Usage

psn_sample(
  edges,
  nodes = NULL,
  consents = NULL,
  desired = NULL,
  dvals = NULL,
  seed = sample.int(.Machine$integer.max, 1),
  shuffle = TRUE,
  carryover = TRUE
)

Arguments

edges

A data frame or matrix whose first two columns are the two endpoints of each tie (one row per tie). Values are converted to character.

nodes

Optional character vector of all node names. Only needed to include isolates, which appear in no row of edges.

consents

Optional named integer vector of consent codes, with the node names as names: 0 = none, 1 = survey only, 2 = survey and photo, 3 = photo only. Every node needs an entry. Only perceivers with code 1 or 2 receive a list, and a pair is eligible only if both nodes have code 2 or 3.

desired

Optional numeric matrix with one row per degree bin and two columns: the number of real and of counterfactual pairs to draw.

dvals

Optional list with one element per row of desired, giving the degree(s) in that bin: a single number, or a vector of consecutive degrees (e.g. 1:2) to merge several distances into one bin. Give desired and dvals together, or neither; with neither, the deployed design is used (degrees 1 to 4, five real and five counterfactual pairs each).

seed

Integer seed for the Julia random number generator. The default is drawn from R's generator, so set.seed() makes results reproducible.

shuffle

Whether to shuffle each perceiver's list (otherwise sorted).

carryover

Whether a bin that falls short is made up from other bins.

Value

A data frame with one row per perceiver and pair: perceiver, from, to (each pair sorted alphanumerically), bin (the degree bin, e.g. "1:2" or "3", as a string) and real (whether the pair is a tie).

See also

psn_inclusion_probs() for the probability that each pair is listed; the Julia package documentation, https://human-nature-lab.github.io/SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
edges <- data.frame(from = as.character(1:20), to = as.character(c(2:20, 1)))
set.seed(1)
lists <- psn_sample(edges)

# merge degrees 1 and 2 into one bin
psn_sample(edges,
           desired = rbind(c(10, 10), c(5, 5), c(5, 5)),
           dvals = list(1:2, 3, 4))
} # }
